title: Rhea Chakraborty Opens Up About Family Toll of Sushant Singh Rajput Controversy
excerpt: The actress revealed that she stopped getting work after 2020 and her brother Showik lost his MBA admission the year he was arrested, as she prepares for her comeback on The Traitors Season 2.
body:
• Rhea Chakraborty revealed she stopped getting acting work entirely after the 2020 Sushant Singh Rajput controversy
  • Her brother Showik had secured MBA admission with 97% marks the same year he was arrested by the Narcotics Control Bureau
  • Their father, retired Lt. Colonel Indrajit Chakraborty, publicly stated the family had been "demolished" by the investigations
  • Rhea is now a confirmed contestant on The Traitors Season 2, which premiered on Amazon Prime Video on August 13

Actress Rhea Chakraborty has spoken candidly about how the controversy surrounding Bollywood actor Sushant Singh Rajput's death in 2020 upended her family's lives, revealing that she was effectively blacklisted from the film industry while her brother lost a hard-won MBA admission.

In an appearance on Neha Dhupia and Angad Bedi's chat show Double Date, Rhea and her brother Showik Chakraborty discussed the difficult period that followed Rajput's death in June 2020 and the subsequent investigations that engulfed their family.

"Nobody Was Signing Me"

"After 2020, I had stopped getting work. Nobody was signing me, and nobody was hiring him either," Rhea said during the interview, according to Filmfare. The statement laid bare the professional devastation the controversy wrought on both siblings.

Showik, for his part, revealed that he had secured admission for his MBA the very same year he was arrested by the Narcotics Control Bureau in September 2020. "I had scored 97 percent marks," he said, reflecting on how dramatically their circumstances changed. Both Rhea and Showik were arrested in connection with a drugs case linked to the Rajput investigation and were later granted bail.

Their father, retired Lieutenant Colonel Indrajit Chakraborty, had issued a public statement at the time of Showik's arrest that captured the family's anguish. "Congratulations India, you have demolished a middle class family," he wrote, according to IANS. "I'm sure next on the line is my daughter and I don't know who is next thereafter."

The CBI Closure and Legal Resolution

The Central Bureau of Investigation, which had taken over the probe from Bihar Police following a Supreme Court order in August 2020, filed a closure report in March 2025. Rajput's lawyer Satish Maneshinde said they were "grateful to the CBI for having thoroughly investigated every aspect of the case from all angles," according to PTI.

In a separate development, the Bombay High Court quashed the look-out circulars (LOCs) that had been issued against Rhea, Showik, and their father, effectively lifting travel restrictions that had been in place since 2020, according to Bollywood Hungama.

Chapter 2: Building a New Identity

Rhea and Showik have since channeled their experience into entrepreneurship, co-founding Chapter 2 Drip, a unisex streetwear brand. The naming process itself reflected their mindset during that period.

"I was very keen on naming the brand Chudail Ka Badla," Rhea said with a laugh during the interview. She also considered "Black Sheep" — "I even got bracelets made with 'Black Sheep' written on them because that's how we felt at the time. We felt like the black sheep of society," she recalled, according to Filmfare.

They ultimately settled on Chapter 2, symbolizing a fresh start. The siblings also co-host the Chapter 2 podcast.

"We felt like the black sheep of society."

— Rhea Chakraborty, on the aftermath of the SSR controversy

The Traitors Season 2 Comeback

Rhea's most visible step back into the public eye comes with her confirmed participation in The Traitors Season 2, the Amazon Prime Video reality show hosted by Karan Johar that premiered on August 13. She joins a cast of 21 contestants including Mallika Sherawat, Munawar Faruqui, Shweta Tiwari, and others in the BAFTA and Emmy Award-winning format.

The show, produced by Dharmatic Entertainment, is an Indian adaptation of the internationally acclaimed reality series. Rhea had previously appeared as a gang leader on MTV's Roadies, but The Traitors marks her first appearance as a full contestant on a reality show.

A Polarizing Figure Returns

The Sushant Singh Rajput case was among the most intensely followed stories in recent Indian entertainment history, generating massive social media campaigns and round-the-clock news coverage in 2020. For the Indian diaspora, the case became a cultural touchstone, with NRIs closely following every development across time zones. Rhea's return to public life — first through entrepreneurship and now through reality television — marks a new chapter for one of Bollywood's most polarizing figures of the last decade.
